# export-attachment: `ExtractOutput`

The `data` payload of `openreadout export FILE --attachment NAME --json`, inside the [envelope](envelope.md).

Output of `export --attachment`.

JSON Schema: [`docs/schema/export-attachment.schema.json`](https://github.com/openreadout/openreadout/blob/main/docs/schema/export-attachment.schema.json) · also printed by `openreadout self schema export-attachment`.

## Fields

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The input file. |
| `format` | `string` | yes | Format id of the input file. |
| `attachment` | [`AttachmentInfo`](#attachmentinfo) | yes | The attachment that was extracted. |

## Types

### AttachmentInfo

A file embedded in the container (thumbnail, label image, time stamps, ...).

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Zero-based index, usable with `export --attachment #<index>`. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | Name as stored in the container (e.g. `Thumbnail`, `Label`). |
| `content_type` | `string` | yes | Content type as the file declares it (e.g. `JPG`, `CZI`, `CZTIMS`). |
| `extension` | `string` | yes | Suggested file extension for the extracted bytes, without the dot. |
| `offset` | `integer` (uint64) or `null` |  | Byte offset of the attachment payload in its file. |
| `size` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Payload size in bytes. |
| `extra` | object |  | Format-specific details in the reader's documented vocabulary. |
